name: survey-confidence-display
description: Validates confidence display: run multiple surveys at different positions, then show the overlay. The confidence markers should appear at each surveyed position with colour-coded indicators (green=high, yellow=medium, red=low). Requires the survey overlay to be wired into syncFromContext().

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a player action: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for the scenario's needs. No role tag -- there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step.

expect.note: level:5 replaces the Rookie starting qualification's proficiency 1

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap — see the assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

Survey 1/4. Surveys are arrival-gated PendingActions (#437), not instant — the surveyor must walk to the site before the result completes, so surveyCount stays 0 through all 4 of these clicks. Each queued survey does cost its SURVEY_COSTS entry immediately, though, which is the real proof this click actually landed.

expect.note: all 4 surveys queued, none completed yet — confirms the arrival-gated system hasn't fired early

at least one of the 4 queued surveys has completed by now (a real run: 3/4 at exactly 53 ticks in command mode) — increased rather than an exact count, since new_game leaves isPaused:false and interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (Finding #12) can complete more of them within the same click round-trip than command mode's headless tick 53 alone

steps.description: Answered through the event dialog's own buttons (EventModal). clickIfPresent, not clickSelector: this step follows a bare tick, so whether an event fired is a random roll and the dialog may not be on screen at all -- the console command it replaced no-ops in exactly that case. When a dialog IS up, a real click has to work, and the usability gate is the same one clickSelector uses, so an inert control still counts as unclickable. Second click dismisses the outcome panel the choice opens.
